newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SACCHI BRINGS BACK OLD MEMORIES AT MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SACCHI BRINGS BACK OLD MEMORIES AT MILAN.

text.p: Arrigo Sacchi has been accused of many things in his time but ageism is not one of them.

The AC Milan and former Italy coach, who celebrated his 51st birthday on April Fools' Day, is set to field a defensive four-man line-up boasting a combined age of 137 years when the champions face league leaders Juventus on Sunday.
Add goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi and it comes to 169.
For those mourning the good old days when Milan won everything, Sacchi seems to have found the answer: Bring back the old players.
The doyen of the team is Pietro Vierchowod, the oldest man in serie A, who can fully expect to mark his 38th birthday in action on Sunday after scoring a goal last month.
The former Sampdoria hard-man, who also helped Juventus capture the European Cup last season, makes Milan captain Franco Baresi look a mere stripling at 36.
Particularly so when placed alongside fellow-defender Mauro Tassotti, who was 37 in January, and is given a reasonable chance of making the start.
The youth in the defence is Italy international Paolo Maldini, still to cross the watershed at 28.
To put it all in perspective, the Milan substitutes are expected to include 20-year-old defender Francesco Coco as well as the more famous 30-year-old Roberto Baggio.
Bearing down on them in the Juventus attack will be Christian Vieri, one of the youngest players in the Italian team at 23 and possibly 22-year-old Nicola Amoruso.
When Baresi made his Milan debut, a club record 522 league matches ago against Verona on April 23, 1978, Coco had just celebrated his second birthday.

When Vierchowod began his remarkable career as a teenager for non-league Romanese in the 1975-76 season, Coco was still the proverbial gleam in his parents' eyes. His professional debut with Como was in 1977, the year of Coco's birth.
"I'll pack it in when I don't feel I am the player I was," Vierchowod said recently, giving the clear impression he felt that day was still some way off.
The Italian with the Russian surname won the league title with Roma.
That fact alone dates him because Roma's only post-war championship win was 14 years ago when Vierchowod's team mates were Brazilian Falcao and current Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti.
He also won the league title with Sampdoria, where he took the Cup Winners' Cup and four Italian Cups.
Then came Juventus and the biggest prize of all.
"It was an important year with Juventus. I would have willingly stayed in Turin and it even looked as it would happen at one point," he recalled.

"They gave me the chance to win the European Cup that escaped me at Sampdoria. Let's not talk about revenge even if it is always stimulating to play against the 'bianconeri'," he said referring to Juventus' black and white stripes.
Ironically, Vierchowod, who walked out on Perugia earlier in the season, was drafted in to the line-up when Baresi picked up an injury -- a case of ring out the old and bring in the older.

The replacement of a 36-year-old with a 37-year-old raised a few eyebrows but the hard-tackling Vierchowod swiftly proved he remains a fighter, something Milan's former ace Marco van Basten found out several years previously to his cost.

Vierchowod's contract expires in June but he remains hopeful it will be renewed. Baresi, credited with much of the improvement shown by Milan since a disastrous start, may decide to retire in June but has yet to announce a final decision.
"I have always got on well with Baresi," said Vierchowod. "We have the experience, but experience is not enough if you are not on form. We are in great form."
